claims.claim: PRIMARY hosted admission binds execution-profile resolution to the trusted policy in the exact carrier checkout, independent of package location and working directory.
REMEDIATION intent hosted admission uses the same explicit trusted policy binding and profile-resolution semantics.
Coding REPAIR hosted admission uses the same explicit trusted policy binding and profile-resolution semantics.
Executor-less REPAIR remains profile-free and does not require the execution-profile policy.
Profile resolution retains omitted, partial, and complete explicit-selection behavior and EXPLICIT versus REPOSITORY_DEFAULT source attribution.
Hosted carriers forward the resolved executor, model, effort, and source tuple downstream without re-resolution or substitution.
The execution-profile policy path comes from trusted carrier context; Issue data does not select it.
Hosted admission fails before downstream dispatch when the trusted policy is missing, malformed, or incompatible, while carrier receipts remain bounded to observed outcomes.
Production-shaped regressions cover explicit canonical policy binding when package-relative policy discovery is unavailable.
The implementation leaves the execution-profile core resolver, self-host workflows, durable dispatch identity, Runtime, Reviewer, Publisher, and lifecycle semantics unchanged.
